literal: Whatever they do not guard, even if, the tongue they should guard; if they do not guard it, they will suffer, having fallen into a slip of the tongue.
translation: Whatever else one fails to guard, one must guard the tongue; if one fails to guard it, one will suffer, trapped by the slip of one's own words.
modern: எவற்றைக் காக்கத் தவறினாலும் நாவையாவது காக்க வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு காக்காவிட்டால், சொற்குற்றத்தில் சிக்கித் துன்பப்படுவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of self-control in speech within the chapter on self-restraint. The author states that even if a person is unable to control other senses or aspects of their life, they must at all costs control their tongue. If they fail to do so, they will inevitably utter harmful or erroneous words. This slip of the tongue will lead to deep regret and suffering, as spoken words cannot be recalled and their consequences are lasting.
